answer.rationale: Finance mandate requires an 18% unit cost cut, and only the low-cost vendor's quote meets that threshold standalone. memory_c2 (verified) confirms the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply last year with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. The contract does not auto-renew, so action is required within 14 days. Deferring risks supply loss. Renewing the incumbent at the current terms does not hit the mandate and memory_c4 shows renegotiation has historically yielded margin gains but not an 18% cut on its own. Switching primary vendor carries delivery risk on a line running at 94% with no buffer, so I will mitigate by making the switch a small, guarded initial allocation rather than a full cutover. Future cycle can layer in a second source (memory_c3) and longer-term commitment pricing (memory_c6) once the low-cost vendor's reliability is confirmed at scale.
